digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest history retention
propositions: Reading all enrichment queue and digest events per ticket during reduce costs O(history) file opens (4,977 opens across 3,727 tickets, breaching 20 ms budget); suffix-lazy newest-first read bounds this to O(dirents + k) where k is failures
Physically deleting committed UUID events violates invariant I1 and triggers git rename detection conflicts in cross-clone merges, even with compaction
Deletion-based retention recovers no repository space (blobs remain in git history) while adding commits and breaking reconvergence, making it cost without benefit
The read bound can be achieved by sorting dirents and reading newest-first per event type, since filenames are monotonic timestamps matching event bodies, requiring no retention or deletion
A merge-safe removal must rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content; fresh-UUID adds paired with deletes will never merge safely
